source_text: Si enim mortui sumus cum Christo, credimus, quia vivemus cum Christo scientes, quia Christus suscitatus a mortuis iam non moritur, mors in eum iam non dominabitur; quod enim mortuus est peccato, mortuus est semel, quod autem vivit, vivit Deo. Ita et vos deputate vos mortuos esse peccato, viventes autem Deo in Christo Iesu [n380] . Quomodo Christus, inquit, qui peccato mortuus est semel, id est propter peccata nostra mortuus est semel, ultra non moritur, sed vivit in gloria Dei, ita et vos, deputate vos peccato mortuos solis vivere et servire virtutibus.
pass_a_gloss: For if we have died with Christ, we believe that we will live with Christ, knowing that Christ raised from the dead already does not die, death will already not dominate over him; for what he died to sin, he died once, but what he lives, he lives to God. So also you, estimate yourselves to be dead to sin, but living to God in Christ Jesus. As Christ, he says, who died to sin once, that is died once on account of our sins, no longer dies, but lives in the glory of God, so also you, estimate yourselves dead to sin to live and serve virtues alone.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5

pass_b_english: ‘For if we died with Christ, we believe that we shall live with Christ, knowing that Christ, raised from the dead, dies no more; death will no longer rule over him. For the death he died to sin, he died once, but the life he lives, he lives to God. So you too reckon yourselves dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus’ (Romans 6:8–11). Just as Christ, he says, died to sin once—that is, died because of our sins once—and dies no more, but lives in God’s glory, so you too, reckoning yourselves dead to sin, should live and serve virtues alone.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian: Paul says death passed to all, not sin; distinguish temporal death from eternal punishment.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
